title: Verifiable Witness Rules for Shot Peening: Strip Bias, Uncertainty, Raster Ripple and Coverage Sampling
content: Shot-peening verification depends on witnesses: Almen strips and coverage checks. Their number, placement and reading are usually set by habit or fixture geometry, and a reported intensity carries no uncertainty. This paper reduces the problem to four claims and an uncertainty budget. Each claim is graded by the strength of its evidence and paired with a test that a shop or laboratory can run. First, strips should come from one recorded lot, because replication cannot beat a lot floor, modelled at 4–6% from the property variation J442 permits (one supplier’s tests show about 1.7%; no between-lot floor has been measured on lot-labelled data). In a modelled budget for a defined current practice, the expanded uncertainty of a reported intensity is about 0.0018 in, comparable with the 0.0015 in verification tolerance, and, in the model, inexpensive controls reduce it about fourfold. Second, on a rastered nozzle a strip shows the exposure ripple multiplied by the saturation slope, so strips are read at or below the characteristic exposure TA. Third, a fast-pass dent track, not a strip, identifies footprint width and divergence. Fourth, coverage should be judged over fields at least 25 dent diameters across, which controls the sampling error of mean coverage between 50% and 98% coverage but cannot find a narrow under-peened band, and exposure read from mid-range coverage. The claims are exact or tested against published data and reduce to placement rules that need no optimiser. The tests that would confirm them in a shop have not been run.
